intro_html: Tender turkey meatballs simmered in a creamy coconut red curry sauce over rice, this is the meal prep that makes coworkers ask questions. Each bowl delivers 37 grams of protein for about $4.18 (at everyday cost), with coconut milk, lime, and ginger doing the flavor work lean turkey cannot do alone.
cost_closing_html: About $4.18 a bowl (at everyday cost) for coconut curry turkey meatballs over rice. A Thai-inspired bowl spot charges $14 for one serving, and theirs has fewer meatballs. We counted.
shop_smart: Ground turkey is the anchor at about $2.68 a pound for the 93/7. It routinely dips on sale below ground beef, and in a curry sauce nobody can tell the difference.

Red curry paste and coconut milk are the flavor engine. One jar of paste covers this batch with room to spare and keeps for months in the fridge, and store-brand coconut milk works just as well as the import for less.
Bread crumbs and eggs are the binder, about $1.50 combined. That is what keeps lean turkey meatballs from turning into hockey pucks, cheapest insurance in the recipe.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice per the package and set it aside.

Mix the ground turkey with the bread crumbs, eggs, garlic powder, ground ginger, dried basil, salt, and black pepper. Do not overwork it, mix just until it holds. Roll into meatballs about the size of a golf ball, roughly 3 per serving.
Brown the meatballs in the vegetable oil in batches over medium-high heat. They do not need to cook through yet, just get color.
In the same pot, cook the onion until soft, then add the garlic, fresh ginger, and red curry paste and fry 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk and stir until the paste dissolves into a smooth, creamy curry sauce.
Return the meatballs, cover, and simmer in the coconut curry until they hit 165F in the center, about 10 to 12 minutes.
Finish with the lime juice and fresh basil, then serve the meatballs and sauce over the rice.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot with rice and meatballs, subtract the empty pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14. Portion to that number and each bowl lands at about 662 calories with 37 grams of protein.

steps: Cook the rice and set aside.
Mix turkey with bread crumbs, eggs, and seasonings, then roll into meatballs.
Brown the meatballs in oil in batches.
Cook onion, garlic, ginger, and red curry paste, then pour in the coconut milk to make the curry sauce.
Simmer the meatballs in the coconut curry to 165F.
Finish with lime juice and basil, serve over rice, and portion into 14 containers.
